newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasani shares up on growth potential.
newsitem.headline: Sasani shares up on growth potential.

text.p: Sasani Ltd shares rose on Wednesday as investors reacted favourably to the stock and management moves in the company, dealers said.
Sasani, quoted in the media sector, reverse-listed into the Crendell cash shell on Monday. It acquired The Video Lab Group which forms its core business.

"The share has picked up dramatically since reverse-listing and volumes are high. Sentiment is positive about this share, pretty much because it is in the same industry with Primedia Ltd," a dealer said.
The share was up eight cents, or 7.84 percent, to 110 cents, after touching a high of 112 cents during the day.
Volumes traded were high with over 2.7 million shares worth over three million rand changing hands. The share was at 90 cents on Friday.
Trade was brisk, leading the JSE's top 10 by moves.
Primedia directors Eric Ellerine and Mervyn King stepped down from that board on Monday due to a potential conflict of interest with their Sasani share holdings.
This showed there was great potential for Sasani, dealers said.
The company is a joint venture between Interleisure Ltd, Video lab Group and a black empowerment group, Msomi Ventures.
Sasani has said in the past that it was looking to expand in the media sector locally and internationally.
"Cash companies hold lots of attractiveness for punters," one dealer said.
